card.occupation: Self-employed electrician (domestic rewires, consumer unit upgrades, kitchen and extension first-fix), regularly working 50–55 hours a week including Saturday mornings
card.education_detail: Finished O-levels and A-levels in Harare, Zimbabwe. Moved to the UK at 19 and worked in warehousing and care work. Later did a Level 2 and Level 3 Electrical Installation course part-time at Gloucestershire College, then his NVQ Level 3 and 18th Edition wiring regulations while working as an improver for a local firm. Went self-employed at 32.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi in Tuffley with his partner Natalie (37, a dental nurse) and her son Kai (13). He and Natalie have been together nine years and keep saying they'll get married 'when things calm down'. They haven't yet. The front drive is mostly taken up by his van.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Harare in a Methodist family. His mum still lives there and his older sister is in Leicester. He came to the UK in 2003 and has been in Gloucester since 2007. He has British citizenship. He grew up on Shona and English at home and still speaks Shona on the phone with family. He goes to a small multicultural evangelical church in the city, more often at Easter and Christmas than week to week, and says his faith is 'there in the background, always'. He feels settled in Gloucester and says 'home' about both places without thinking about it.
card.professional_persona: Good on the tools and great with customers. He chats to everyone and gets a lot of repeat work and word-of-mouth jobs. He's weak on admin: invoices go out late, his van is a mess of offcuts and receipts, and he books jobs back-to-back so one overrun knocks the whole week. Natalie nags him to do his VAT and he usually leaves it until the week it's due. He's calm when things go wrong on site and doesn't stress about tight deadlines, which customers find reassuring.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Arsenal fan from watching the Premier League on TV in Harare. He watches matches at the pub with a couple of mates when he can. He played five-a-side on Wednesday nights for years and still turns up roughly every other week. He'll go to a Gloucester Rugby game if someone has a spare ticket and enjoys the atmosphere more than he follows the rules.
card.arts_persona: Music is the main thing. He plays Oliver Mtukudzi and old Zimbabwean sungura in the van alongside Afrobeats, gospel and whatever's on Heart Radio. He doesn't read much beyond the odd autobiography of a footballer. He watches action films and series with Natalie and Kai on a Sunday night and laughs loudest in the room.
card.travel_persona: Tries to get back to Zimbabwe every two or three years to see his mum, usually for three weeks over Christmas, and takes Natalie and Kai when they can afford it. Otherwise it's a week in Spain or a caravan in Devon or Cornwall in the summer. He's not a planner: Natalie books everything and he packs the night before.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks sadza with beef stew or greens when he's homesick and has taught Kai to like it. Most weekdays it's whatever's quick: meal deals from the Co-op at lunch, a takeaway on Fridays. He does a big barbecue in the garden whenever the weather allows and invites half the street. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'.
hobbies_and_interests: WhatsApp groups with family and old school friends
going to church at festivals and family occasions
skills: talking to customers and calming them down
getting on with pretty much anyone
card.career_goals: Wants to take on an apprentice in the next year or two and maybe grow into a small firm with a second van. He knows he'd need someone else, probably Natalie, to sort the books. He's also thought about doing EV charger and solar installation courses because 'that's where the work's going'.
card.voice: Warm, loud and quick. He's chatty from the first sentence. His Zimbabwean accent is still clear but softened after 20 years in Gloucestershire, and he says 'alright' and 'cheers' like a local. He uses 'you know' and 'yeah' as tags a lot and says 'sort of' when explaining. He hesitates with a short 'er' rather than 'erm'. He laughs easily, often mid-sentence. He doesn't really leave silences. If there's a pause he fills it with a story or a joke, and he'll pick up the interviewer's words and run with them. If he mishears, he says 'sorry, say again?'
card.typing: Fast and careless. Mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only sometimes. Apostrophes are often missing (dont, im, its). He uses few commas and joins ideas with 'and' or a dash. He writes the odd 'lol' or 'haha', and 'tbh' now and then. Answers are short unless he gets going on something he cares about. He rarely goes back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open. He asks the other person questions back, makes jokes, and treats a research call like a chat in someone's kitchen. He isn't nervous or guarded. He's happy to give opinions, but he isn't pushy and will laugh off disagreement. He can drift off-topic and need steering back.
small_things: his van's heater has been broken since November
Kai has grown out of his football boots again
a customer in Quedgeley who wouldn't stop making him tea
the price of copper cable lately
the barbecue he's planning if the weather holds
deeper_things: he misses his mum and worries about her getting older so far away
his dad died when he was 24 and he couldn't afford to fly back for the funeral
his first few years in the UK, working nights in care homes and feeling invisible
he sometimes wonders why he and Natalie haven't married and suspects it's mostly him putting it off
he thinks of Kai as his son and quietly hopes Kai thinks of him as his dad
faith got him through the hard early years even if he doesn't go to church much now
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, set on a kitchen table, framing Tendai from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. It's evening, and the main light is a warm overhead kitchen bulb, which puts a slight shine on his forehead and leaves the left side of his face a bit shadowed. He's a Black man of about 40 with a broad face, a short neat beard flecked with a little grey at the chin, and a closely cropped haircut. He has no glasses. He's grinning widely, mid-laugh, with his eyes creased. He's wearing a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered logo reading 'TM Electrical' on the chest, and there's a faint smudge of plaster dust on one shoulder. Behind him is a fitted kitchen with white gloss cupboards and a grey worktop, a kettle, a toaster, a stack of post and receipts beside a fruit bowl holding two bananas, and a school timetable and takeaway menus stuck to the fridge with magnets. A hi-vis jacket hangs over the back of a chair visible at the right edge of the frame.
